stem: A client receiving bevacizumab (AVASTIN) is scheduled for elective major surgery. Which preoperative medication plan is consistent with the current prescribing information?

options.A: Withhold bevacizumab for at least 28 days before the elective surgery
options.B: Continue bevacizumab through the day of surgery because it does not affect wound healing
options.C: Hold bevacizumab only on the morning of surgery
options.D: Increase the bevacizumab dose before surgery to reduce postoperative bleeding

rationale: AVASTIN is associated with surgery and wound-healing complications. Current labeling instructs clinicians to withhold AVASTIN for at least 28 days before elective surgery. It also states not to administer AVASTIN for at least 28 days following major surgery and until adequate wound healing. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Apply the labeled perioperative bevacizumab safety rule: withhold AVASTIN for at least 28 days before elective surgery because of wound-healing complications.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_locator: §2.1 Dosage and Administration: withhold for at least 28 days prior to elective surgery; do not administer for at least 28 days following major surgery and until adequate wound healing; §5.2 Surgery and Wound Healing Complications
source_claim_supported: Bevacizumab should be withheld for at least 28 days before elective surgery because of surgery/wound-healing complications; post-major-surgery administration is also delayed until at least 28 days and adequate healing.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16: identify medication precautions/contraindications, adverse effects, and safe administration
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — bevacizumab perioperative wound-healing precaution
correction_summary: Replaced the vague statement that bevacizumab is held for an unspecified period because of bleeding/wound risk with the exact current labeled preoperative interval. Retained the wound-healing rationale and avoided conflating it with a universal bleeding-only mechanism.
audit_findings: A exactly matches the current AVASTIN label. B and C provide insufficient withholding and contradict explicit instructions. D is the opposite of safe practice and has no pharmacologic rationale. The stem specifies elective major surgery and AVASTIN, eliminating ambiguity about emergency procedures or other bevacizumab products. One best answer remains; the 28-day threshold is directly source-supported.
